text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp. said Tuesday it has completed its $3.9 billion acquisition of Infinity Broadcasting Corp., creating a radio powerhouse.

The Federal Communications Commission approved the transaction Thursday, completing the approval process. The deal had already been approved by the Justice Department and Westinghouse and Infinity shareholders.

Westinghouse, the owner of CBS Inc., said the merger creates a CBS Radio group with total revenues of about $1 billion. The group will have 79 radio stations in 17 markets, including New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Philadelphia, Boston, Washington and Detroit.

Infinity Broadcasting President Mel Karmazin will lead the radio group, the companies said. Karmazin and CBS Inc. President Peter Lund will also serve in the office of chairman, formed by Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan.
Pittsburgh-based Westinghouse in November announced plans to spin off its $4.6 billion industrial business in 1997, leaving a media-centred company behind.
